headline: House Opens Scrutiny of Proposed ₱7.2-Trillion 2027 National Budget
seoTitle: House Opens Scrutiny of ₱7.2-T 2027 National Budget | FMB News
seoDescription: The House began scrutiny of the proposed ₱7.2-trillion 2027 national budget, with flood-control spending and public-service delivery among the issues under review.
deck: The proposed spending plan is now under congressional review, with lawmakers examining how major allocations translate into public services and disaster resilience.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The FMB News overnight brief reports that the House of Representatives opened scrutiny of the proposed 2027 National Expenditure Program after its submission to Congress.

The overall proposed budget is ₱7.2 trillion. That total is independently supported by the Development Budget Coordination Committee's July fiscal-program statement and by subsequent reporting on President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.'s 2027 budget proposal.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The National Expenditure Program is the executive branch's proposed spending plan. It is not yet the final General Appropriations Act and remains subject to congressional deliberation, amendment and approval.

The newsroom brief says early questioning included flood-control spending, education needs and agency capacity to carry out funded programs. FMB News is treating those hearing details as source-attributed reporting rather than expanding them beyond what can be independently confirmed.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The annual budget determines how public money is distributed across education, infrastructure, health, social protection, agriculture, security and other government functions. Scrutiny of implementation capacity matters because appropriations alone do not guarantee that projects will be completed on time or deliver their intended results.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch the House Committee on Appropriations for agency-by-agency hearings, proposed amendments and the timetable for moving the General Appropriations Bill to plenary debate. Also watch for official DBM budget tables that clarify final proposed allocations by department and program.
